_comment: The half of the colophon that CANNOT be derived. Every binding this Worker declares needs an entry here, and every entry needs a binding. The measurements are transcribed from the specs that ruled them (Capsid's search-architecture.md and media-module-architecture.md, and build-history.md) and must not be invented here.

d1:DB.what: SQLite at the edge. Holds every post, the tag graph, the derived search corpus, the media index and the llms.txt row.
d1:DB.whyLoadBearing: The media index lives here because R2 paginates in key order and promises nothing else. Sort by date, filter unused, search by name, count by type: each is a query, and building one over a key-ordered iterator means listing the whole bucket per request. A capability decision, not a scale one.

kv:APP_KV.what: The Ask answer cache keyed by a SHA-256 of the normalized question, plus short-lived state: the health snapshot, draft preview tokens, the editor divergence flags and the drift counts.
kv:APP_KV.whyLoadBearing: The cache sits in front of the daily ceiling rather than behind it, so a repeated question costs nothing and consumes no budget. The ordering is the design: a hit reaches no model.

r2:MEDIA.what: Uploaded originals, content-addressed as sha256(bytes) truncated plus the extension.
r2:MEDIA.whyLoadBearing: Content addressing was decided on security, not tidiness. The old key was derivable from public information, so a draft's images were reachable by guessing a slug the sitemap publishes plus eight hex characters.

r2:OG.what: Social cards, one per post, rebuilt by command, and the CV's PDF, one object replaced each time the CV is saved.
r2:OG.whyLoadBearing: A second bucket exists because the two split on LIFECYCLE rather than on what the UI calls them. MEDIA is irreplaceable; OG is regenerable, so it is safe to empty and is deliberately outside the backup path.

r2:MEDIA_REVISIONS.what: Every earlier version of an uploaded file, kept when a replace, turn or resize overwrites it, so the editor can put any of them back.
r2:MEDIA_REVISIONS.whyLoadBearing: MEDIA holds only the current bytes of each file, so an overwrite would lose the old ones. They are kept here before the write, and no code path deletes from this bucket; check:destructive sweeps for one. It is separate from MEDIA so the media library lists only current files.

r2:BACKUPS.what: Nightly dumps of every D1 table, one folder per run, each finished by a completion marker, kept 14 daily, 8 weekly and 6 monthly, and a nightly copy of MEDIA and MEDIA_REVISIONS. Every night a job outside Cloudflare copies all of it to Amazon S3.
r2:BACKUPS.whyLoadBearing: D1 is derived from the repository except for a handful of tables nothing can rebuild: webmentions, the sealed procedure versions, the Knowledge Base inventory and the lab roster with their audit trails. A dump is the only copy of those rows, and the file copies are the only copies of the uploads outside their buckets. wrangler d1 export cannot do the job because D1 refuses to export a database holding an FTS5 table.

ai_search:AI_SEARCH.what: Retrieval and answer generation for Ask, on built-in storage with uploaded markdown rather than the crawler.
ai_search:AI_SEARCH.whyLoadBearing: It sits above classic search rather than replacing it, because the two fail on OPPOSITE inputs. Measured on the same corpus: classic found 2 things AI retrieval missed, all exact tokens, and AI retrieval found 3 that classic missed, all natural-language questions. Neither layer subsumes the other.

durable_object:ASK_BUDGET.what: The per-IP burst limit and the site-wide daily ceiling for Ask, on the synchronous SQLite storage API.
durable_object:ASK_BUDGET.whyLoadBearing: Both cheaper mechanisms were built first and both leaked. The GA ratelimit binding, configured at 5 per 60 seconds and attacked with 12 concurrent requests, refused 1, then 2, then 9, then 0 across four runs. A Durable Object using async storage.get then storage.put allowed 8 through a ceiling of 3, because a read and a write spanning an await is not atomic. The synchronous API allowed exactly 3, which is why the class is registered as new_sqlite_classes.

ratelimit:CSP_REPORT_RATE_LIMIT.what: Sixty CSP violation reports a minute per caller address, the same limit every site in the network sets on the report sink its gateway answers.
ratelimit:CSP_REPORT_RATE_LIMIT.whyLoadBearing: The sink is a public POST that anyone can call, and the limit keeps a flood out of the logs. A report over the limit is dropped and still answered 204. The binding's count is loose (see ASK_BUDGET), which costs nothing here, because a dropped report loses nothing a later one will not repeat.

images:IMAGES.what: Thumbnail and content-width transforms, computed on request from the original. Written back only when an editor turns or mirrors a picture, or uploads one larger than the library keeps, and then the earlier bytes are kept.
images:IMAGES.whyLoadBearing: The BINDING and not the /cdn-cgi/image/ URL syntax, and that is forced rather than preferred: the URL interface answers 404 on both of this site's addresses, with Cloudflare error 1042 on the workers.dev address (which has no zone) and a plain 404 on dustinedwards.info, so the binding is the only route to resizing.

ai:AI.what: Workers AI, which suggests tags and alt text for a picture when an editor asks for them in the media library. Nothing it says is saved until a person accepts it.
ai:AI.whyLoadBearing: Alt text is the step most often skipped, and a plain first draft of it makes the step quick. The call runs through AI Gateway when one is configured, with request and response bodies kept out of its logs, and only an editor's own uploads are sent, never anything from a visitor.

browser:BROWSER.what: A headless browser that prints the CV to PDF. The Worker calls it after each CV save and keeps one PDF in the derived bucket.
browser:BROWSER.whyLoadBearing: The CV is edited through Carrel and goes live with no deploy, so a PDF committed to the repository went stale on every save and failed CI until someone re-rendered it by hand. The PDF is derived from the CV rows, so it is rendered where the rows live, stamped with a fingerprint of the data it was drawn from, and a health check compares that fingerprint with the CV the site shows. A failed render never undoes a save: the check goes red and the watcher re-renders.

version_metadata:CF_VERSION_METADATA.what: The time the running version was uploaded. /health's cron check reads it and nothing else does.
version_metadata:CF_VERSION_METADATA.whyLoadBearing: A scheduled job added after its hour has not been due yet, and without the deploy time /health warned that it never ran. With it, a job is expected only once its first window since the deploy has passed, so the warning means a trigger really is missing.

send_email:EMAIL.what: Email Sending from the Worker, used once a day at most: when ORCID or Crossref lists a paper of Dustin's that the publications list does not have yet, the DOI is mailed to him once.
send_email:EMAIL.whyLoadBearing: A new paper is added through Carrel by hand, so nothing on the site notices one by itself. The mail is what turns a paper published elsewhere into a line on this site, and each DOI is mailed once so a paper waiting to be added is not mailed every day.

assets:ASSETS.what: The static files under public/, served without a Worker invocation.
assets:ASSETS.whyLoadBearing: The binding has exactly one method, fetch(), so a Worker can serve any path it is given and discover none of them. That is why the media rebuild reads a committed manifest: the one thing it cannot do for itself is find out which static files exist.

queue_consumer:dustinedwards-media-event.what: R2 event notifications from both buckets, consumed to derive the media index rows.
queue_consumer:dustinedwards-media-event.whyLoadBearing: The write path is a notification into a queue, never a dual write. The Worker writes only to R2 and the consumer re-derives the row from the object as it is now, never branching on what the message claimed, which is what makes replay and out-of-order delivery converge.

queue_producer:WEBMENTION_VERIFY.what: The webmention endpoint's producer: one message per accepted mention, carrying the row id, source and target.
queue_producer:WEBMENTION_VERIFY.whyLoadBearing: The endpoint answers 202 only after the send lands, and 503 if it fails, so the sender retries rather than a row waiting on a verification nobody will run. Absent on a Worker Preview, which cannot consume a queue, so the endpoint refuses there.

queue_consumer:dustinedwards-webmention-.what: Webmention verification: the row id the endpoint sends after it writes the unverified row, consumed to fetch the source and record the verdict.
queue_consumer:dustinedwards-webmention-.whyLoadBearing: A verification cut short in waitUntil was lost; here it is retried and then kept in the dead-letter queue. The consumer re-reads the row and fetches nothing unless it is still unverified, so a redelivery is a no-op.

notAdopted.name: Vectorize
notAdopted.reason: Rank fusion over two FTS5 indexes answers this corpus in about fifteen lines and no vectors. Zero-result queries are the cheapest content-gap signal the site has, and the only evidence that would justify reopening the question.

notAdopted.name: Images storage
notAdopted.reason: Transforms are used; storage is not. It bills in $5 increments per 100,000 stored images, for a library of dozens.

notAdopted.name: Soft delete and a trash prefix
notAdopted.reason: A team concern. The audience is one person, and R2 wins every conflict already, so a deleted row that should not have gone is restored by the next rebuild.

notAdopted.name: Media versioning
notAdopted.reason: Keys are content-addressed, so a changed image is a different key by construction. Versioning would be a second mechanism for something the addressing already does.

notAdopted.name: Single-flight on Ask
notAdopted.reason: Declined with the bound written into the route. Deduplicating identical questions does not lower the worst case: N addresses spend the same N units asking N DIFFERENT questions. The 200 per day ceiling is the real bound and it is exact.
